Verder ontwikkelen, inrichten en positioneren van de Chief Privacy Officer-functie.

Functioneel aansturen van privacyfunctionarissen en privacyaanspreekpunten binnen de organisatie.

Adviseren van hoger management over complexe privacyvraagstukken.

Opstellen, uitvoeren en bewaken van het privacyplan.

Doorontwikkelen van privacy governance, privacybeleid en bijbehorende processen.

Uitvoeren, begeleiden en beoordelen van Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIA's).

Eisen

Afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding op het gebied van gegevensbescherming, privacy of een vergelijkbare richting.

Minimaal 2,5 jaar aantoonbare ervaring als Chief Privacy Officer (CPO) of plaatsvervangend CPO binnen de Rijksoverheid.

Aantoonbare ervaring met de toepassing van privacywetgeving, waaronder de AVG, binnen grote organisaties met meer dan 1.000 medewerkers.

Aantoonbare ervaring met functionele aansturing van privacyfunctionarissen of privacyadviseurs.

Aantoonbare ervaring met het ontwikkelen of doorontwikkelen van privacy governance en privacybeleid.

Aantoonbare ervaring met het adviseren van hoger management over privacyvraagstukken.

Pré

Relevante privacycertificering, zoals CIPP/E of CIPM.

Ervaring met het uitvoeren of beoordelen van DPIA's.

Ervaring met het opzetten, vastleggen, inrichten en vervullen van een CPO-functie.

Ervaring met privacygerelateerde audits en onderzoeken.

Ervaring met Privacy by Design binnen organisatieprocessen of digitale producten.

Kennis van en/of ervaring met de EU AI Act en de relatie tussen AI-governance en privacy.

Overtuigend en verbindend.

Bestuurlijk en organisatiesensitief.

jobs.description:
Title: Interaction Designer (Contract)

Bungie is seeking an Interaction Designer to delight millions by designing amazing player interactions within Marathon. You’ll be responsible for producing UX design work on a cross functional team, evolving problems that are complex and ambiguous into clear actionable design solutions. You'll work from concept to completion by collaborating closely with other designers to achieve your goals.

Responsibilities

  • Convert goals and requirements into viable solutions that follow and complement our UX strategy and design principles.
  • Utilize appropriate UX design methodologies to communicate and validate the player experience: player interviews, flow diagrams, playtesting, high-fidelity mockups, and prototypes.
  • Establish and document strategies, guidelines, and patterns.

Required Skills

  • Effective collaborator: You know how to move a design forward with your team and in discussions with stakeholders using proven collaboration methods.
  • User-centered designer: You are a committed believer in putting player needs at the center of the development process. You know how to incorporate both qualitative and quantitative insights into your design process.
  • Visual communicator: You have comprehensive knowledge of graphic design fundamentals like layout, color theory and typography.
  • Process and team driven: You can break experiences down with a team to ship value to our players. You embrace that an effective user experience needs feedback and iteration to achieve.
  • Systematic thinker: Your design process considers moderate-to-large scale solutions that are sustainable over time.
  • Experience working on a cross-functional product team.
  • A portfolio with UX projects.

Nice-to-Have Skills

  • Degree in Human-Computer Interaction, User Experience, Cognitive Science or equivalent.
  • Experience in games across multiple platforms.
  • Ability to use design software (Figma, Adobe Suite, etc.) to convey designs.
  • Experience with player onboarding systems.

jobs.title: Ingénieur PS Zero Trust / SASE (Cloudflare One)
jobs.description:
À propos de Brixio  Brixio est un partenaire spécialiste de Cloudflare : intégration, services professionnels et services managés sur l'ensemble de la plateforme, de la sécurité applicative au SASE. Brixio est partenaire Cloudflare certifié ASDP et fait partie depuis juillet 2026 du groupe Equans (groupe Bouygues), 18,7 Md€ de chiffre d'affaires et environ 85 000 personnes.  L'équipe compte une trentaine d'ingénieurs répartis entre Paris, Dubaï et un centre de production à Casablanca. Les clients sont des grands comptes et des ETI en France, en Europe et au Moyen-Orient, ainsi que les entités du groupe Equans.  La mission  L'ingénieur PS Zero Trust / SASE déploie Cloudflare One chez les clients français de Brixio, du cadrage technique à la mise en production. Il devient la référence opérationnelle Zero Trust de l'équipe France et prend en charge les projets SASE dès son arrivée, notamment le déploiement interne de Cloudflare One chez Brixio et l'accès distant sécurisé aux sites industriels du groupe Equans.  Il travaille avec le Delivery Manager France, qui pilote le planning, le budget et la relation projet, et avec l'architecte principal, référent technique de l'équipe.  Responsabilités

Cadrage :  animer les ateliers techniques avec les équipes réseau, sécurité et poste de travail du client, puis rédiger le design détaillé (architecture d'accès, politiques, plan de migration).

Déploiement Cloudflare One :  Access (ZTNA), Gateway (SWG et filtrage DNS), client WARP, Tunnel, CASB, DLP, isolation de navigation (RBI), et selon les projets Magic WAN, Magic Firewall et Email Security.

Migrations :  remplacer les VPN par du ZTNA et les proxies existants par Gateway, sans rupture de service pour les utilisateurs.

Intégrations :  fournisseurs d'identité (Entra ID, Okta) en SAML, OIDC et SCIM, contrôles de posture (Intune, EDR), remontée des logs vers le SIEM du client.

OT et industrie :  sécuriser l'accès distant des prestataires et techniciens aux équipements industriels et techniques.

Sécurité des usages IA :  appliquer les contrôles Cloudflare One aux usages de l'IA (détection du shadow AI, DLP sur les prompts, gouvernance des applications IA).

Livraison et passation :  documentation (HLD, LLD, runbooks), recette avec le client, passation au support et au MSP de Casablanca.

Rigueur projet :  travailler dans le périmètre signé, signaler au Delivery Manager toute demande hors périmètre avant de la traiter, et saisir son temps chaque semaine dans Brixio One.

Industrialisation :  contribuer aux modèles de déploiement réutilisables (configurations types, Terraform, playbooks) pour accélérer les projets suivants.

Requirements

Profil indispensable  Le poste demande d'être opérationnel sur le SASE dès les premières semaines. Sans expérience SASE en production, la candidature ne sera pas retenue.

SASE en production :  au moins 2 ans de déploiements Zero Trust / SASE chez des clients, sur Cloudflare One, Zscaler (ZIA, ZPA), Netskope, Palo Alto Prism

jobs.title: Consultant senior / Manager - Conseil en transformation, organisation et gestion de projet
jobs.description:
Pourquoi ce poste existe maintenant  Ad Valoris change de modèle. Depuis vingt ans, nous aidons des directions générales de Suisse romande, publiques et privées, à voir clair, à décider et à embarquer leurs équipes. Depuis 2025, nous pratiquons le conseil augmenté : l'IA nous sert à comprendre mieux, à aller plus loin, pas seulement à produire plus vite.  Le cabinet est en pleine croissance : de nouvelles directions nous confient leurs enjeux et un deuxième bureau ouvre à Lausanne. Nous cherchons deux personnalités prêtes à rejoindre cette aventure humaine : une équipe dynamique et engagée, au sein de laquelle vous pourrez contribuer au développement du cabinet et tracer votre propre parcours.  Ce que vous ferez  Vous rejoignez le cabinet comme consultant-e senior ou manager, selon votre expérience. Sur un mandat, vous pouvez assumer plusieurs responsabilités ; en particulier, vous concevez la démarche de chaque mandat, vous vous assurez qu'elle répond au vrai problème du client et vous gérez la relation avec lui tout au long de la mission.

Comprendre avant de proposer. Lire la situation du client, ses acteurs et ses non-dits, avant d'arriver en séance.

Résoudre le bon problème. Remettre en cause la commande quand elle ne vise pas le vrai sujet, et défendre une recommandation engagée.

Co-construire et faire avancer. Apporter tôt une première version, la faire travailler par le client jusqu'à ce qu'il en soit co-auteur, et animer seul-e des séances, y compris sur des sujets complexes, dans des environnements exigeants et avec des parties prenantes aux sensibilités diverses.

Créer de la valeur pour le client. Mieux comprendre, aller plus loin dans l'analyse et concrétiser : ce qui compte, ce sont les progrès durables que le client constate dans son organisation.

Faire grandir le cabinet. Transmettre, challenger et accepter de l'être.

Deux points d'entrée, selon votre expérience :

Manager (dès 10 ans d'expérience). Architecte de mission dès votre arrivée : vous cadrez et pilotez des mandats de bout en bout, et vous encadrez un ou deux consultants en continuant à produire. Vous prenez part à la conduite du cabinet : méthodes, recrutement, capitalisation. Trajectoire explicite vers un rôle où vous portez le résultat et la croissance de plusieurs comptes.

Consultant-e senior (dès 5 ans d'expérience). Autonome sur un périmètre cadré, vous menez vos entretiens et ateliers seul-e ou en équipe, et vous êtes une référence en conseil augmenté. Trajectoire explicite vers le rôle d'architecte de mission.

Le conseil augmenté, tel que nous le pratiquons  Le conseil augmenté, ce n'est pas utiliser l'IA pour produire plus vite. C'est l'utiliser pour comprendre mieux, sans jamais laisser la production avancer plus vite que la compréhension. Le test est simple : qu'avez-vous fait du temps que l'IA a libéré ? Plus de livrables, c'est de la sous-traitance à une machine. Plus de présence chez le client et plus de profondeur d'analyse, c'est du conseil augmenté

Every change to Anthropic's software has to reach production somehow: new code, runtime configuration, feature flags, infrastructure changes. Our team builds the systems those changes travel through. Our mission is to give every team at Anthropic a fast, safe, and predictable path from change to production.

We sit within Anthropic's Infrastructure organization and own pipelines, staged rollouts, health-gated promotion, and rollback, along with runtime configuration, feature flags, and the systems that deliver code and artifacts to machines across a very large fleet. We are an AI company operating at the cutting edge of the industry, growing quickly in a fast-moving environment. As we scale and prepare for a future IPO, we are building our Procurement function from the ground up. We're a smart hydration company rebuilding an industry that still runs on sugar water and single-use packaging.
Filtered water, functional flavors, zero bottles. Still, sparkling, cold, and hot. All poured from one tap. We create hydration people want to reach for, starting with the workplace where we help teams thrive.

jobs.title: Anthropic Research Resident

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

The Anthropic Residency is our paid, fixed-term research program, with placements lasting between six weeks and six months. We are looking for people who have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields and want to transition to full-time work focused on making sure AI systems are safe and beneficial for all of humanity. If you are a professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer and want to transition to work on transformative AI, we want to hear from you. Background in machine learning is not required.

  • A concrete, scoped project matched to your background, with direct mentorship from Anthropic researchers
  • Access to Claude models and GPU compute
  • Connection to the broader AI safety and security research community

Interview process

Applications for this round close on November 22, 2026 (11:59 PM PT). We expect to make offers in January 2027.

  • Are motivated by making sure AI is safe and beneficial for society as a whole
  • Are excited to transition into working on empirical AI research full-time
  • Have led ambitious work in a variety of technical fields (professor in a quantitative discipline, a technical founder or a staff-level engineer)
  • Thrive in fast-paced, collaborative environments
  • Can implement ideas quickly and communicate clearly

Strong candidates may also

  • Have experience authoring research papers in machine learning, NLP, or AI safety
  • Have experience with LLMs, reinforcement learning or Kubernetes clusters and complex shared codebases

Mentors and research areas

Potential Anthropic mentors include:

  • Sara Price: leads the Alignment Training team; background in data science
  • Ethan Perez: leads the Alignment Science team; background in machine learning
  • Evan Hubinger: leads the Alignment Stress-Testing team; formerly at The Machine Intelligence Research Institute (MIRI)

jobs.description:
Location(s):  US (remote), Boston (hybrid), or New York (hybrid) -  EST preferred

Toast  is expanding into the B2C market and is looking for a Brand Experience Designer to define and build the consumer-facing brand that millions of diners will come to know. This role is critical for turning a fledgling brand into one that feels distinct, trusted, and alive at every touchpoint, across product and marketing. The Brand Experience Designer will shape how the Consumer brand looks, sounds, and behaves end to end, setting the standard for how Toast shows up to guests and giving the product and growth teams a shared identity to build on.

Toast is investing in becoming a consumer innovator. We’re using our restaurant and guest data to make dining feel personal and frictionless, and with AI in the mix, we want discovery, booking, and dining to feel genuinely memorable. Our Toast Local app is only one surface. We’re adding social features, exclusive deals, and new ways to reserve and pay. A brand that guests recognize and love is how that experience becomes more than a set of features.

About the team

You’d join a small, ambitious Consumer Design team that feels and operates like a startup within a larger company. We have autonomy and the runway to reimagine dining, and we all love to roll our sleeves up and jam together. You’ll report to the Consumer Product Design leader and work shoulder to shoulder with product designers, product managers, engineers, and our marketing and growth partners.

The competition is fierce. We’re up against established brands consumers already recognize. We’re building so that consumers and restaurants thrive and form deep relationships that keep dining a core, sustainable business in our communities. With a brand still finding its shape and a nimble, driven team raring to go, this role is where the brand gets its voice.

The Consumer brand is a sibling to the Toast Core brand, not a sub-brand of it. We honor what makes Toast trusted by restaurants, and we give guests something that feels made for them. What’s shared and what’s distinct is still being decided, and this role helps decide it. If you want a brief with every answer already in it, this isn’t that role. If you want to shape the answers, it is.

About this roll* (Responsibilities)

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
Make security the reason people trust Ockto

Own security at the platform people use to share their most personal data

Every day, people use Ockto to share their identity, income, assets and bank data: when they apply for a mortgage, rent a home or take out a lease. Banks and other large organisations choose Ockto partly because of the level of assurance we offer around that data. At Ockto, security is not a support function. It is part of the product and organisational culture.

As our CISO, you make sure it stays that way as we grow. Part of that growth is adopting an AI driven operating model with strong guardrails. You own Ockto's security programme, from risk and controls to incidents, suppliers and audits. You set the standard, check that it is met, and make security measurable in a way that the whole organisation (and specifically our engineers and spec leads), clients, auditors and regulators all recognise. You do this with a real mandate and short lines to the people who decide.

What you'll do  You own the information security programme of a supervised financial company and make it work in daily practice, not just on paper. As CISO, you:

Own Ockto's ISMS and security policy framework, and keep our ISO 27001 certification (held since 2017) and our SOC 2 assurance current and credible.

Translate the risk appetite set by management into a security strategy, an annual plan and clear standards that teams can build to.

Keep Ockto ahead of what's coming. You track developments such as eIDAS2 and the EU Digital Identity Wallet, NIS2, the Cyber Resilience Act and the AI Act, assess what they mean for Ockto and our clients, and translate them into our security strategy and standards in time.

Verify and challenge. Our engineering teams operate the technical controls; you check that they work and that findings get fixed. You approve risk acceptance for serious vulnerabilities and commission penetration tests. All control owners are challenged and prepared to show evidence and reproduce controls.

Lead the response to security and privacy incidents, approve notifications to regulators, and make sure root causes lead to structural fixes.

Manage security risk in our supply chain, from onboarding new suppliers to the annual review of critical ones, in line with DORA.

Make sure our continuity and recovery arrangements are tested and hold up, together with Engineering.

Make security measurable. We judge it by how quickly and how structurally we resolve what we find, not by counting incidents.

Represent Ockto's security towards clients, auditors and supervisors: from a bank's due diligence questionnaire to our external audits and contact with DNB and AFM.

Build a security-aware culture with an awareness programme people actually remember.

Who you work with  You report to our Product & Trust Director, who sets Ockto's trust framework and risk appetite. Within that framework, the security strategy and its execution are yours. On security matters

Your job is to keep that promise true in the real world: triaging InfiniBand issues when prefill and decode nodes stall exchanging KV cache over RDMA, diagnosing hero-model and LoRA-serving faults that don't show up in generic health checks, and extending the automated self-healing system so each new failure mode becomes a permanent fix instead of a recurring page.

The core value we're after is keeping the decoupling real even when things break, and keeping the fleet efficient without that efficiency becoming a new source of instability. You'll own SLOs and error budgets for inference serving, lead incident response, and turn what postmortems teach you into actual changes in the controllers and automation, not just updated runbooks. You'll also work the reliability side of capacity efficiency, since a mistuned defragmentation or bin-packing pass is itself a production risk. Strong candidates have hands-on production-reliability experience on large-scale distributed or GPU-serving systems, are comfortable troubleshooting InfiniBand/RDMA and Kubernetes controller/CRD-based platforms, and think about GPU infrastructure, and the tools that keep it reliable, as software to be engineered.

A product mindset applies: the on-call experience, the clarity of an alert, and the judgment built into an automated remediation are things you ship and iterate on.

  • Triage and extend automated self-healing: when the node-scanning and remediation platform misses something, a new failure mode, an InfiniBand issue in disaggregated prefill/decode serving, a GPU Xid variant, a hero-model or LoRA-specific fault, diagnose it live, drive the fix to production, and turn it into a new detection/remediation plugin so it's automatic the next time.
  • Own end-to-end reliability of the pipeline: hold the SLOs and error budgets for provisioning and fleet health, lead incident response when idempotency, retry, rollback, or drift assumptions break down in practice, and drive the systemic fix, not just the hotfix.
  • Partner with the inference/ML platform team from the production side: be the one who knows how real cluster

jobs.title: Creative Advisor - Human Frontier Collective
jobs.description:
About the Collective

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC)’s mission is to bring the world's best minds to shape the future of AI. As a Creative Advisor, you’ll bring your creative practice into direct collaboration with Scale’s research and ML teams. You’ll help them understand how work gets made in your field, develop new work together, and provide feedback on how AI models support—or fall short of—real creative processes.

What You’ll Do

  • Connect with other creators: Meet and learn from creatives and researchers across HFC and your industry.
  • Shape work in your domain: Share the taste, judgment, methods, and creative decisions behind your practice to help inform model development.
  • Create alongside the team: Collaborate on briefs and develop new work that helps explore what models can and cannot do in your field.
  • Partner with ML and research teams: Define what “good” looks like in your field, review model outputs, flag where AI falls short, and give feedback that shapes how models learn your craft.
  • Help peers understand the opportunity: Introduce other creators in your field to the program and share your experience contributing work.

Who Should Apply

We’re looking for leading creators in their field who are interested in shaping AI and how it’s changing creative work. No AI experience needed. Your expertise in your craft matters most, and being connected to others in your field is a plus. This is a paid, part-time role with a flexible schedule.

Why Join

  • Have a voice: Contribute your subject-matter expertise and perspective in your domain. Build the future by shaping frontier models.
  • Collaborate across disciplines: Work with ML and research teams and connect with other leading creatives.
  • Explore new creative possibilities: Make new work through paid, commissioned briefs that challenge what models are capable of doing.
  • Get paid for your expertise: Paid $300 hourly, with compensation, time commitment, and project scope shared during your interview.

Application Process

  1. Apply: Share your background and a link to your portfolio. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
  2. Portfolio Review: Share one past project you’re proud of. Nothing is used without a signed agreement and payment, and we’ll follow up with next steps.
  3. Meet the Team: A paid conversation with our research and ML team to walk through your work.
  4. Get Started: Successful candidates are invited to join the Human Frontier Collective as a Creative Advisor.

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager, Accessibility
jobs.description:
About Us

Twitch is the world’s biggest live streaming service, with global communities built around gaming, entertainment, music, sports, cooking, and more. It is where thousands of communities come together for whatever, every day.

We’re about community, inside and out. You’ll find coworkers who are eager to team up, collaborate, and smash (or elegantly solve) problems together. We’re on a quest to empower live communities, so if this sounds good to you, see what we’re up to on LinkedIn and X, and discover the projects we’re solving on our Blog. Be sure to explore our Interviewing Guide to learn how to ace our interview process.

About the Role

As the Senior Program Manager, Accessibility at Twitch, you will have a broad impact across all of Twitch and our Community. Reporting into the VP of UX, you will join our Design team where you will own the program design, education and enablement, and the auditing and testing output. We will look to you to execute the vision of how Twitch will be a welcome home for all regardless of abilities. You will partner with product, design, engineering, and legal to solve accessibility problems at scale and provide strategic solutions.

You can work from Twitch’s headquarters in San Francisco, CA; or from one of our hub locations in Seattle, WA; Los Angeles, CA; Irvine, CA; or New York City, NY - with West Coast (PST) working hours.

  • QA & Testing: Lead QA execution and manage QA specialists and third-party vendors; partner with engineers to build automated accessibility testing into CI/CD pipelines, shifting testing earlier in the development lifecycle.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Frontier AI is on track to be among the most consequential and most adversarially-targeted technology in the world. The capability curve is steep, the adversaries who want these systems are extremely well-resourced, and the security bar this will eventually require is well beyond where the industry operates today. Incremental hardening alone is not going to close that gap, so we need breakthroughs and a group of people to go find them.

Security Labs is that team. We run a portfolio of high-risk, high-expected-value security projects: the work that seems impractical until someone optimistic and stubborn enough actually tries it. Projects run on the order of weeks rather than quarters, and each one is either handed off to the Anthropic team that will own it in production or wound down with a writeup of what we learned. We expect a meaningful fraction of our bets not to land.

This team is intentionally scrappy and ambitious. We're intentionally iterating fast on high-risk research bets and we expect a meaningful fraction not to land. If a 30% project success rate sounds uncomfortable, or uncharted and chaotic territory isn’t both frightening and exciting, this probably isn't the right fit. There are other places in Anthropic Security doing important work with more structure, less risk, and more certain paths to positive outcomes.

The questions we're trying to answer include:

  • Can our core research workflows survive extreme isolation?
  • Can we replace trust with cryptographic guarantees?
  • Can the models themselves become our most effective security control?
  • What would it actually take to defend against a tier-1 state adversary, and how much of that can we build now?

Who we're looking for. We're hiring generalists with rare depth. You're a strong software engineer as a baseline, and on top of that you've gone deep in at least one area most engineers don't get near: firmware or hardware security, applied cryptography, OS / kernel / hypervisor internals, formal methods, reverse engineering, or high-assurance and cross-domain systems. You've built things under your own direction, you're comfortable jumping layers when the problem demands it, and you'd rather take a swing at something that might not work than ship the safe incremental thing. jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is an AI safety and research company working to build reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our customers and society as a whole. As an Enforcement Analyst focused on Agentic Alignment, you will play a crucial role in identifying and investigating harmful and unexpected behavior by models, and make enforcement decisions accordingly. You'll work closely with a suite of cross-functional teams, within and outside of Safeguards, including: Policy, Threat Intel, Engineering, Research, and Transparency. Your work will be essential in maintaining Anthropic's commitment to safe and beneficial AI as Claude takes on more autonomous work.

Important context for this role: In this position you may be exposed to and engage with explicit content spanning a range of topics, including those of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature. There is also an on-call responsibility across the Policy and Enforcement teams.

Key responsibilities

  • Review and investigate potential instances of Agentic Misalignment, working from transcripts, tool-use traces, and code
  • Triage cases by severity and urgency and share through the appropriate channels
  • Help operationalize review pipelines for agentic cases, translating leads from detection outputs and investigations into structured review workflows that scale
  • Make enforcement decisions under the Usage Policy, applying it consistently to novel agentic scenarios and across surfaces, and documenting the reasoning behind each decision
  • Assess cyber-related agentic activity, such as scanning, exploitation attempts, credential misuse or malicious code to determine its real-world harm potential
  • Write clear, well-evidenced case write-ups for audiences ranging from enforcement peers to senior leadership
  • Identify patterns and trends across cases, and close the loop between enforcement outcomes and upstream improvements by feeding findings back to policy, detection and research teams to improve policies, classifiers and model behavior
  • Maintain rigorous documentation of enforcement decisions, review logic and precedents to build institutional knowledge
  • Collaborate with Threat Intelligence, Research, Engineering and Policy partners so that detection coverage keeps pace with how agentic misuse and misaligned behavior evolve
  • Use AI systems, including Claude, to accelerate your ow

Anthropic's Safeguards team plays a critical role in ensuring our AI systems are deployed safely, responsibly, and in line with our values.

jobs.title: Design Engineer - Canada
jobs.description:
Hi  I’m

Abhik  ,  Ashby 's Co-Founder and VP of Engineering. This role is close to my heart because, as someone who can both design and code, it’s where I’ve always done my best work, but also where I was seen as a rebel and an outsider. I want folks like me to feel at home at Ashby, and so I made Design Engineering a formal role and department that works closely with me. Our first hire was over five years ago, and we’re doubling the team from five to over ten in the next year.

This role truly expects you to design and code. Design Engineer at Ashby isn’t just a Frontend Engineer with new branding, nor is it a Designer vibe coding prototypes. Combining excellence in both is where magic happens. I found that when I put my best effort into both the design and technical implementation of a feature, I had a nimbleness and creativity that was hard to achieve when I did only one or the other. For instance, the UX and UI I envisioned often influenced the data model's design and flexibility, while the understanding of technology's capabilities often simplified or improved the design. This role embraces that.

You’ll work on our most challenging design problems, help others improve their designs by expanding and enhancing our in-house design system, and consult on bespoke design work needed by Product Engineers. To ground it with examples, Design Engineers at Ashby have:

Redesigned our mobile web app by talking with customers who use it often, wireframing new flows, implementing its design system, and using that system to turn the wireframes into a polished UI.

Built a set of flexible, composable components in our design system that allow other engineers to build beautiful, consistent setup wizards across our product easily.

Helped a Product Engineer improve the information hierarchy and scannability of their design for viewing a candidate’s assessments. Recruiters can quickly parse information and pick out anomalies.

The Design Engineer role is more common today than five years ago, but I believe Ashby offers a unique opportunity that few can match:

You work on a product at scale, not at an early-stage startup struggling to find users and get feedback on what you’ve designed and built. At Ashby, your work will touch over 100,000 weekly active users, millions of candidates per week, and notable customers like Notion, Linear, Shopify, and Snowflake. You’ll get to test out ideas with our own recruiting team and hiring managers who use Ashby every day (like me), and often hear customer feedback as early as the day you release.

jobs.location: US - Culver City, California, United States
jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Tax Manager to join our Finance team in Culver City, California, on a hybrid basis, working two days per week from our office.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play, every day — whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues, or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

Show us the money! As the Finance team, we're number crunchers with top-notch analytical and reporting skills. As a shared service, we get to work with all of Scopely's talented studios.

As Scopely continues to grow its global footprint and portfolio, we are seeking a Tax Manager to join the Finance team. Reporting to the VP, Global Tax, this role will help manage Scopely’s domestic and international tax matters across compliance, provision, planning, reporting, and risk management.

The Tax Manager will be a hands-on partner to the business, working closely with Finance, Accounting, and other teams to translate tax requirements into practical, scalable processes and advice. This is an opportunity to help shape a high-performing global tax function in a fast-moving interactive company.

What You Will Do:

  • Own the day-to-day coordination of Scopely’s tax compliance calendar, partnering with external advisors and internal stakeholders to deliver timely, accurate federal, state, local, and international filings, estimates, extensions, and payments.
  • Prepare or review quarterly and annual income tax provision calculations and related disclosures under ASC 740, including current and deferred tax, effective tax rate analysis, return-to-provision items, and cash tax summary.

jobs.description:
MaintainX  is a leading mobile-first work execution platform  for industrial and frontline teams.  More than 13,000 customers , including Duracell, McDonald's, Shell, DHL and Volvo, use MaintainX to cut unplanned downtime and run better operations, across 13.9 million managed assets and 79.5 million completed work orders.

In August 2026 MaintainX became part of Autodesk, joining

Autodesk Operations Solutions

, the organization unifying Autodesk's operations platform alongside Tandem, FlexSim and Fusion Operations.  Autodesk's strategy is to converge design, make and operate into one continuous lifecycle: design an asset, build it, run it, then feed what you learn running it back into the next design. Autodesk had design and make. Operate is the phase that tells you what actually happened, and it is ours.

Role context

This role sits on the Brand Design team inside Marketing, the brand and motion designers behind our campaigns, web, launches and events. Every piece of that work moves through Asana, and this person owns how it comes in, how it moves and how it ships. You'll be the reason designers spend their days designing.

The role

You will own the operating rhythm of the Brand Design team, from the moment a request lands to the moment the work ships.

Own intake in Asana.  Review new requests with Marketing stakeholders, make sure each arrives with a complete creative brief, and prioritize what the team takes on, cutting the back-and-forth that pulls designers away from design.

Build and maintain the processes  that move work smoothly from request to delivery, consistently adapting and optimizing.

Partner with Marketing Program Management  on large marketing initiatives each year that touch every marketer, setting start dates and deliverable milestones with clear reasoning behind them.

Track team capacity against demand  and raise trade-offs early, so deadlines are decisions rather than surprises.

Keep project files and deliverables organized  so anything the team has made can be found in seconds.

Build the reporting  that shows what the team delivers and the impact of that work, in both qualitative and quantitative terms.

You'll report to our Director of Marketing Creative, and work alongside a team of designers and motion designers.

About you

You've run project delivery for an in-house creative, design or marketing team.

You've owned intake and set the standard for a good brief, and you've gotten requesters to follow it.

You're fluent in a work management tool. Asana is ours.

You plan across many teams, set milestones, and turn scattered feedback into clear next steps.

You notice what's broken before anyone tells you and arrive with a proposed fix.

You influence through rationale, data and diplomacy, and you're clearly on your stakeholders' team. People want to work with you because you serve the company as a whole rather than defending any one group.

Nice to have

Experience reporting on the outcomes of creative work with

jobs.description:
Synthesia  is the world’s leading AI video platform for business, used by over 90% of the Fortune 100. Founded in 2017, the company is headquartered in London, with offices and teams across Europe and the US.

As AI continues to shape the way we live and work, Synthesia develops products to enhance visual communication and enterprise skill development, helping people work better and stay at the center of successful organizations.

Following our recent Series E funding round, where we raised $200 million, our valuation stands at $4 billion. Our total funding exceeds $530 million from premier investors including Accel, NVentures (Nvidia's VC arm), Kleiner Perkins, GV, and Evantic Capital, alongside the founders and operators of Stripe, Datadog, Miro, and Webflow.

The role:

We're looking for a Staff (L6) Product Designer to lead design for some of Synthesia's AI-native, agentic Sessions product surfaces.

Sessions are the experiences where employees learn through conversation, companies lrun a survey at scale, and AI becomes a direct participant in how work gets done - not just a tool behind the scenes.

This area is central to redefining what a video platform can be: moving upstream from content creation into workforce development, and making complex AI capabilities feel natural, trustworthy, and effective for everyday users.

You'll operate as a senior IC: setting direction, influencing roadmap decisions, shaping bets with Product and Engineering leaders, and raising the craft bar.

In practice, this role is about solving AI-native design problems, for example:

Designing real-time, conversational avatar experiences that feel engaging and natural - not robotic or gimmicky - for employees learning and practising skills at work.

Creating interaction patterns for AI-driven workflows that give users the right amount of control, transparency, and trust without overwhelming them with complexity.

Improving output quality through better structure, guidance, and feedback loops - helping users understand what the AI is doing, catch issues early, and iterate with confidence.

Working at the frontier where AI changes what "interaction" means, and the best patterns are genuinely still being invented.

In this role you will:

Own major AI-native bets end-to-end, from problem framing to shipped outcomes and iteration.

Set a design vision for our "Sessions" surface, and influence adjacent product areas to stay coherent.

Partner closely with Product and Engineering to define what "great" looks like (principles, quality bar, success metrics) and then drive toward it.

Prototype and test interaction models quickly - including novel agentic and conversational patterns - and know when high-fidelity matters.

Raise the bar on craft: interaction design, UI quality, systems thinking, and consistency across AI-native experiences.

You should apply if you bring:

Significant experience designing complex, high-usage product surfaces - ideally including AI-native produ

jobs.title: Senior Product Designer
jobs.description:
RevenueCat  gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile.

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance.

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The Role

As a Senior Product Designer at RevenueCat, you’ll own complex product problems from discovery through production. You’ll work closely with Product and Engineering to understand customers, identify opportunities, shape what we build and why, and turn technically complex workflows into simple, polished experiences for developers.

You’ll join a small design team with a high bar for interaction and visual craft. We’re looking for someone who is comfortable with ambiguity, talks directly to customers, prototypes and iterates quickly, and stays involved until the work is shipped and working well in production.

About you

You have a strong track record solving complex product problems in B2B, SaaS, developer tools, or similarly complex environments.

You can frame ambiguous problems, identify opportunities, make sound trade-offs, and help shape what gets built and why.

You design clear, intuitive workflows and think carefully about information architecture, states, edge cases, errors, and interactions.

You have a high visual craft bar and care deeply about hierarchy, typography, spacing, composition, and polish.

You stay close to customers, using direct conversations and qualitative and quantitative evidence to inform your decisions.

You work closely with Product and Engineering, involve partners early, reduce scope intelligently, and stay engaged through implementation and follow-up.

You communicate clearly in a remote, asynchronous environment and take ownership beyond the boundaries of a design handoff.

You understand technical constraints well enough to make realistic decisions and are comfortable using prototypes, code, or modern AI tools when they help you learn or move faster.

You are excited about our mission to help developers make more money.

Get to know our product, customers, and teams.

Familiarize yourself with our design system and visual language.

Talk to some customers to understand their needs.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer, Post-Training
jobs.description:
About the role

As a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) focused on Post-Training, you will be a hands-on technical partner to our most strategic customers: AI teams using fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to build differentiated models on open-source foundations. FDE does not replace our Solutions Architects. You will work alongside them as the deep-domain specialist in post-training, guiding customers through data strategy, algorithm selection, experiment design, and evaluation, and sizing the compute behind it. You’ll make sure we can deliver on our post-training POCs, drive adoption of our fine-tuning and RL platform, and turn customer goals into measurable gains in model quality. Your work directly affects customer success, company growth, and the hardening of our core platform.

Responsibilities

  • Data Strategy: Help customers define and execute their data strategy for model post-training, diagnose data quality issues that limit model performance outcomes, and provide recommendations for data generation for post-training scale
  • Algorithm Selection: Recommend the right post-training approach for each use case
  • Experiment Design & Hyperparameter Tuning: Design well-controlled experiments and tracking methods; diagnose training instabilities, reward hacking, and regressions.
  • Evaluation: Build evaluation frameworks with customers, including task-specific benchmarks, LLM-as-judge pipelines, and held-out test sets. Make sure gains are reproducibly aligned with production success metrics.
  • Model Selection: Guide base model selection methodology ahead of post-training efforts and baseline quality evaluations to guide post-training objectives. Interest in self-directed research of newly released open source models, particularly as they relate to post-training.
  • RL Workload Sizing: Scope and size RL and fine-tuning workloads, partner with sales and capacity teams to shape deals and capacity forecasts.
  • Strategic Customer Alignment: Serve as the primary post-training technical point of contact for aligned strategic accounts. Lead technical execution from scoping to production and make sure we hit critical milestones.
  • Product & Research Feedback Loop: Shape our fine-tuning and RL product roadmap with insights from the field. Contribute code, recipes, and reference implementations where needed, and drive early adoption of new features and research with strategic logos.

Requirements

  • Experience: 5+ years in a technical role in ML engineering, Applied AI, Forward Deployed Engineering, or Solutions Architect, with recent hands-on experience post-training LLMs.
  • Post-Training Depth: Expert-level, hands-on experience with fin

Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team brings Claude to organizations doing some of the world's most important work across the nonprofit and education sectors. These organizations share a problem: mission-critical work, thin budgets, and little slack to figure out new technology on their own. Our Customer Success team helps them go from first login to Claude being part of how their teams work, but we cannot do that one organization at a time, nor should we. The sector already has trusted intermediaries these organizations turn to first: networks, capacity builders, funder technical assistance providers, community colleges, and fellowship programs. This role exists to make those intermediaries as effective at activating and training organizations on Claude as our own Customer Success team is.

As the Scaled Enablement Lead, you'll build the Claude for Nonprofits train-the-trainer program that qualifies intermediaries to onboard organizations and deliver Anthropic-designed workshops on our behalf. You'll own the kits, credentials, and quality gates that let them run the show without an Anthropic CSM in the room. You'll also own the enablement thinking behind scaling impact through Claude Corps: how what fellows learn and build serves every organization we support, not only the ones that host them.

The people you enable are not selling Claude. They are trainers, implementers, and program staff whose job is to help mission-driven organizations meaningfully adopt AI. Your job is to make sure these intermediaries can do that with Claude, to the same bar we hold ourselves to, and to help them evolve their offerings as we learn what these organizations need. The measure of success for this role is organizations activated and trained well without Anthropic delivering it.

You'll be half program builder, half facilitator. You'll write the performance requirement and verification method behind each control, review every site design against them at each stage with redlines a design team can act on, test in the field that what was built performs as specified, and re-verify post-acceptance changes.

This is a foundational role. You'll own Anthropic's physical security reference design package (typical details, reference drawings, schedules, and test procedures) in the form partners build from, and keep it current against each site's threat basis and the sites actually being built. You'll set the technical position for a site and decide what applies where; where a requirement can't be met as written, you'll engineer the compensating control and document the deviation. You'll work with the rest of DCSE, with Anthropic's design, construction, and real estate counterparts, and directly with the vendors who build to the package. This role involves regular travel to data center sites. These are critical services, and this role participates in an on-call rotation for them.

jobs.title: Regional Research Economist, Economic Research
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Regional Research Economist at Anthropic, you will collaborate with governments, academia, industry, and civil society in your region to measure and understand AI’s effects on the economy and explore research-driven policy interventions. You will contribute to the development of the Anthropic Economic Index and its extension to generate regionally relevant insights, establish new methodologies to measure the usage, diffusion, and impact of AI throughout the economy, and work to broaden access to and usage of the insights generated by the Index. You will use frontier methods in econometrics, machine learning, and structural estimation. Such rigor will drive impact, shaping both policy discussions externally and informing Anthropic’s internal business and product decisions.

Our team combines rigorous empirical methods with novel measurement approaches. We’re building first-of-its-kind datasets tracking AI’s impact on labor markets, productivity, and economic transformation. Using our privacy-preserving measurement system (Clio), we analyze millions of real-world AI interactions to understand how AI augments and automates work across different occupations and tasks.

For this role, we’re looking for candidates who can combine rigorous economic analysis with novel measurement approaches to understand AI’s transformative effects on the economy. The ideal candidate will be comfortable working at the intersection of empirical economics, technological change, and policy impact.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and maintain relationships with academic institutions, policy think tanks, and other research partners as the primary point of contact for these organizations on economic impact work in your region
  • Advance research collaborations that answer country- or regional-specific economic impact questions
  • Translate research insights into actionable recommendations for policy discussions
  • Make fundamental contributions to the development and expansion of the Anthropic Economic Index, including country- and regional-specific analysis
  • Design and collaborate on empirical research on AI’s economic effects with governments, academia, industry, and civil society in your region
  • Develop new methodological approaches, in collaborat

We are seeking a hands-on Engineering Manager to lead our Frontier AI Infrastructure team within Public Sector Engineering. This is a 50/50 role: you'll spend roughly half your time writing and reviewing code, and half your time leading, coaching, and growing a small team of engineers.

jobs.title: Forward Deployed Product Manager, Enterprise

Role Summary

Scale is accelerating the development of AI across the world's most important organizations. The Forward Deployed PM is the person who makes enterprise deployments succeed from the product side — embedded with customers, shaping real production outcomes, and translating messy operational reality into high-signal input for the core platform.

This is not a roadmap PM, a CSM, or a solutions engineer. The FDPM owns product outcomes inside a portfolio of enterprise accounts: earning deep trust with senior customer stakeholders, driving deployments to production, identifying where the product is the bottleneck vs. execution, and feeding durable, specific signal back to the platform team. The best FDPMs have shipped products into large organizations and can tell the difference between a customer's stated request, their actual problem, and what the platform should do.

What You'll Do

  • Own product outcomes for our highest impact enterprise accounts. You are the accountable PM for product delivery and customer value.
  • Build trusted advisory relationships with VP/C-level buyers and senior technical leads. Become the reliable escalation point on the Scale side before issues surface externally.
  • Drive deployments from contract to production. You have done this before for large organizations. You know what 'production-ready' actually means and you close the gap.
  • Translate real customer workflows, friction, and priorities into high-signal product input for core platform teams. Not requirements docs — specific, evidence-backed product perspective with tradeoffs articulated.
  • Distinguish where the product is the constraint from where execution, integration, or change management is. Drive each type of blocker to resolution through the right channel.
  • Partner closely with FDEs so the account runs as a coordinated team, not a set of parallel workstreams.
  • Identify and develop expansion opportunities grounded in demonstrated customer value
  • Represent customer reality to platform and leadership with enough credibility that it changes decisions.

What We're Looking For

Core Competencies

  • Enterprise deployment ownership: has driven AI/ML or complex software products from contract to production at scale, with real integration, real security constraints, real change management.
  • Product judgment in the field: translates customer reality into product direction, not just feature requests; can say no credibly and explain why.
  • Customer trust-building: earns and maintains trust with demanding senior stakeholders over multi-quarter engagements; manages conflict without eroding the relationship.
  • Technical translation: bridges the gap between customer engineering teams and Scale platform engineers; does not relay messages, adds interpretation.<

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Public Sector
jobs.location: Denver, CO; Honolulu, HI; Washington, DC
jobs.description:
The goal of a Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to leverage techniques in the fields of generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI to improve Scale's products and customer experience in production environments. Our machine learning engineers take advantage of robust internal infrastructure and unique access to massive datasets to deliver improvements to our customers.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with a strong focus on both large language models and computer vision. On the LLM side, we are developing agentic systems that help solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners. This includes building agent frameworks that integrate with custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, as well as evaluation tools to benchmark and refine agent behavior. We're also advancing research in areas like reinforcement learning for agentic LLMs, with successful deployment into real-world operational environments. On the computer vision front, we're training advanced models to increase labeling throughput and automate perception tasks. Our efforts include building large-scale fine-tuning pipelines, training models across multiple modalities, and developing generalizable vision foundation models to support a wide range of defense applications.

You will:

  • Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community, use them in production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
  • Improve and maintain production models through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
  • Collaborate with product and research teams to identify and prototype ML-driven product enhancements, including for upcoming product lines
  • Work with massive datasets to develop both generic models as well as fine tune models for specific products
  • Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
  • Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
  • Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs

This role will require an active TS security clearance

  • 2+ years of experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production envir

jobs.title: Machine Learning Fellow - Human Frontier Collective
jobs.description:
About the Collective

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC)’s mission is to bring the world's best minds to shape the future of AI – because the future of AI depends not only on powerful models, but on the people who teach them to think.
We bring together researchers, academics, and domain leaders across 70+ fields – over 90% of members hold doctorates – to shape how frontier AI systems are built, evaluated, and governed. HFC members have since co-authored published work including SciPredict, PropensityBench, and Professional Reasoning Benchmark.

Why join the HFC

HFC centers on three core pillars: the network itself, participation in selected AI/ML projects, and opportunities to publish with our research team.

  • Join a unique and exclusive expert network: You’ll become a part of an interdisciplinary community, consisting of over 90% doctorates and field leaders representing 70+ fields from the leading institutions. We’re a collective of top innovators and thought leaders committed to advancing frontier AI to power the world’s most important decisions.
  • Participate in AI/ML projects: Beyond the collective network, you’ll be regularly invited to work on high-impact projects with Scale AI and its affiliated lab and platform: building AI safety and policy guardrails, helping models understand real-world deep learning workflows by designing, reviewing, and optimizing PyTorch models, evaluating complex ML code and AI-generated implementations for efficiency and correctness, and more.
  • Co-author selected research publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers—boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition.

Who should apply

  • Background: PhD, or postdoctoral research experience, in Machine Learning, Computer Science, or a related field; or senior industry experience in Machine Learning or a related field.
  • Skills: Strong proficiency in Python and modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow). Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS) and MLOps tools (Docker) and LLM frameworks (LangChain) is a plus.
  • Professional Mindset: Detail-oriented, innovative thinker with a passion for applied AI research and a commitment to collaboration.

How it works

  • Duration: This is a fully remote opportunity with no fixed end date; engagements continue as long as there's mutual interest. This is a 1099 independent contractor engagement.
  • Work authorization:

jobs.title: Machine Learning Research Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. Our products provide the high-quality data and full-stack technologies that power the world's leading models, and help enterprises and governments build, deploy, and oversee AI applications that deliver real impact. We work closely with industry leaders like Meta, Ernst & Young, Mayo Clinic, Time Inc., the Government of Qatar, and U.S. government agencies including the Army and Air Force.

Scale's Machine Learning Research team builds the foundation for the next generation of AI systems — pushing the boundaries of what's possible with frontier models while ensuring safety, reliability, and alignment at every step. Our work spans generative AI, reinforcement learning and advanced post-training methods, scalable oversight, synthetic data pipelines, red teaming, and evaluation science.

We are developing a large-scale hybrid human-machine system to power machine learning pipelines for dozens of industry-leading customers. These models and systems form the backbone of Scale's long-term strategy, enabling billions of tasks monthly and supporting some of the most complex and advanced use cases in the AI ecosystem.

As an intern, you'll work on a combination of deeply technical ML applications in production and cutting-edge research problems, with mentorship from world-class researchers and the opportunity to collaborate with leading teams across industry and academia. Interns own real, published or shipped work — not side projects.

Example Projects

  • Measure the dangerous capabilities of frontier models and conduct preparedness research
  • Research the science and creation of new benchmarks for frontier models
  • Develop new methods for training models to excel on extremely difficult reasoning problems that require long chains of thought
  • Research reinforcement learning and post-training methods that improve model reliability on high-stakes tasks
  • Research scalable oversight protocols that enable humans to produce and quality control reasoning chains beyond their native capabilities
  • Study the boundaries of model generalization and capabilities to inform data-driven advancements
  • Research synthetic and hybrid data with humans in the loop to scale up high-quality data generation
  • Take models currently in production, identify areas for improvement, improve them using retraining and hyperparameter searches, then deploy without regressing on core model characteristics
  • Create post-training or agentic solutions that integrate into our ability to deliver applications for enterprise and public sector clients

Required to Have

  • Currently enrolled in a BS, MS or PhD program with a focus on Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or Natural Language Processing, with a graduation date in Fall 2

jobs.title: Machine Learning Research Scientist, Evaluations
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; New York, NY
jobs.description:
Scale works with the industry's leading AI labs to provide high quality data and accelerate progress in GenAI research. We are looking for Research Scientists and Research Engineers with expertise in LLM post-training (SFT, RLHF, reward modeling) and evaluation. This role is on the evaluation pod within the GenAI Research Organization and will focus on building benchmarks and diagnosing model failure modes in both text and multimodal modalities.

In this role, you will develop rigorous evaluations and diagnostic methods that reveal where frontier models fail and why. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to define best practices in evaluation-driven AI development. You will also partner with top foundation model labs to translate failure analysis into technical and strategic input on the next generation of generative AI models.

You will:

  • Analyze model behavior to identify, characterize, and diagnose failure modes in frontier LLMs and Agents. You’ll identify everything from capability gaps and reasoning errors to robustness and alignment issues, all focusing on RCA.
  • Design and build benchmarks and evaluation methods that measure LLM capabilities in both text and multimodal modalities.
  • Apply post-training expertise (SFT, RLHF, reward modeling) to connect observed failures to the data and training interventions that address them.
  • Publish research findings in top-tier AI conferences.

Ideally you’d have:

  • Ph.D. or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, or a related field.
  • Deep understanding of deep learning, reinforcement learning, and large-scale model fine-tuning.
  • Experience with post-training techniques such as RLHF, preference modeling, or instruction tuning, and with LLM evaluation or benchmark development.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Published research in areas of machine learning at major conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, CVPR, etc.) and/or journals.
  • Previous experience in a customer facing role.

jobs.title: Product Manager, Enterprise Core Platform
jobs.location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
Role Summary

Scale is building the agentic operating system that powers AI deployment across the world's most important organizations. The Platform PM is the person who determines what that foundation needs to be — and holds the bar on how well it gets built.

This is not a roadmap PM, a program manager, or a feature tracker. The Platform PM owns the core infrastructure that every FD team builds on top of: defining the foundation before anything else can be built reliably, sequencing work against real customer commitments and FD team velocity, identifying which FD-built patterns are ready to graduate to core, and ensuring that every capability that ships does so at a bar customers can trust without thinking about it.

The best Platform PMs have defined platform capabilities at production bar in high-stakes environments and understand the difference between what is necessary to build, what is interesting to build, and what should never be built at all.

What You'll Do

  • Define the foundation. Determine what needs to be true at the core platform layer — across each capability pillar — before anything reliable can be built on top of it.
  • Sequence it. Prioritize and order platform work given customer commitments, FD team velocity needs, and what is actually blocking progress today. Getting this wrong means building on an unstable base or building the right things in the wrong order and paying for it in rework and FD team drag.
  • Identify patterns and graduate capabilities. Watch what FD teams are building across the application layer, determine what is genuinely repeating, and make the call on what moves to core — and when. Do not rush graduation or delay it out of caution.
  • Hold the quality bar. Every capability on the platform roadmap earns its place twice: once by being necessary, and again by being done well enough that customers trust it without thinking about it. Keep the platform from becoming a graveyard of half-built capabilities.
  • Unlock delivery team time to value. Forward deployed delivery teams should spend their time solving the hardest customer problems, not rebuilding plumbing on every engagement. That requires a platform that is secure by default, deployable anywhere, observable in production, and equipped with the agentic primitives, eval infrastructure, expert judgment capture, and data reasoning capabilities that every agent workload needs.
  • Partner across the organization. Work closely with platform engineering, forward deployed PMs, and BU leads to surface signal, resolve sequencing tradeoffs, and keep the roadmap grounded in what is actually blocking work.

What We're Looking For

Must-Have Qualifications

  • 6+ years in product management with meaningful time owning platform, infrastructure, or developer-facing products at production bar.

jobs.description:
About Scale

Scale builds AI systems for decisions that matter. We started out providing the data and evaluation behind many of the world's leading models, and we still work with the major frontier labs on research and post-training. Today we also build full applications: we take an organisation's own data and expertise, forward deploy alongside their teams, and build the systems they come to rely on, powered by the Scale GenAI Platform.

The Role

The UK is making a wholesale shift to AI. The government's AI Opportunities Action Plan set out to "mainline AI into the veins" of the country, and the focus has now moved to delivery: the Incubator for AI (i.AI) is shipping tools like the Humphrey suite into departments, a Sovereign AI Unit and AI Growth Zones are being stood up, and civilian departments are under real pressure to move from pilots to production. Scale can play a foundational role in building the reliable AI applications that shift depends on.

We're looking for someone to lead that work in central government. This isn’t about staying in the office and managing a team of sales people, its about building the business from the front. You'd own our commercial relationships across civilian departments, starting where the near-term pipeline is strongest: HMRC, DWP, and NHS.

This is a critical role reporting directly to our Head of Public Sector, UK. You'd carry a number, win deals yourself, and build a small team behind you as the work grows. It suits someone who has sold into these departments before and knows how they actually make decisions, not just how the org charts look.

What you'll do

  • Own our commercial plan and pipeline for UK civilian central government
  • Find, shape, and close deals yourself, from the first conversation through to contract and into delivery
  • Use the relationships you already have across departments like HMRC, DWP, and NHS
  • Work the frameworks, tenders and teaming, and know which route to market is worth the effort and which isn't.
  • Be a credible counterpart to senior civil servants, and turn what they need into work we can deliver
  • Stay close to our product and delivery teams so what we sell is what we build
  • Hire and lead a small team over time, and help shape the wider UK public sector plan with the UK Public Sector Lead

What we're looking for

  • You've sold and delivered technology or transformation work to UK civilian central government, either from a vendor or from inside government
  • You’ve rolled up your sleeves and built something from scratch, whether that’s a new vertical, territory or product launch
  • You know at least one major department well (e.g. HMRC, DWP, or NHS) and how it buys
  • You understand public sector procurement: frameworks, tenders, and buying that runs through a lot of stakeholders
  • You've opened door

jobs.title: Research Advisor - Human Frontier Collective (UK)
jobs.description:
About the Program

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings together top researchers and domain experts to collaborate on high-impact work that are shaping the future of AI. As an HFC Research Advisor, you’ll apply your academic and professional expertise to help develop strategy, design, evaluate, and interpret advanced generative AI systems – while gaining exposure to cutting-edge research and working alongside an interdisciplinary network of leading thinkers.

What You’ll Do

  • Senior Advisory & Model Governance: Provide elite-level consultancy and leadership on model behavior and domain-specific logic, establishing the benchmarks for professional integrity.
  • High-Impact Research Collaboration: Influence the technical roadmap by partnering across Scale AI's product, research, delivery, and GTM teams to design sophisticated, small-scale tasks that translate expert-level intuition into rigorous, computable frameworks for frontier model evaluation.
  • Executive Client Engagement: Represent Scale AI and the HFC as a Subject Matter Expert during pivotal sales cycles, executive meetings, and conferences,
  • Visionary Creation: Contribute to the creation of premier technical content and strategic GTM assets that ultimately helps position Scale as the definitive leader in the industry.
  • Publications: Collaborate with Scale’s research team to co-author technical reports and research papers, boosting your academic visibility and professional recognition (e.g., SciPredict, PropensityBench, Professional Reasoning Benchmark).
  • HFC Community: Become a foundational member of HFC; a supportive, interdisciplinary network of innovators. Gain exclusive access to a community of industry leaders and AI researchers dedicated to advancing the frontier of data.

Who Should Apply

    • Finance: IB/PE/VC/consulting C-Suite, VPs, or Directors from Bulge Bracket or Elite Boutiques (e.g., Goldman Sachs, Blackstone), Senior Managers, Senior Associates, or Senior Analysts from top-tier firms.

    • Medical: Board-certified MDs from premier academic hospitals (e.g., Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic). Practicing physicians w/ at least 5 YOE of post-residency experience from premier hospitals.
  • Professional Experience: 5+ years of relevant industry experience with strong, top-tier domain knowledge

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Agent Robustness
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA; New York, NY
jobs.description:
Scale Labs, Research Scientist — Agent Robustness

As the leading data and evaluation partner for frontier AI companies, Scale plays an integral role in understanding the capabilities and safeguarding AI models and systems. Building on this expertise, Scale Labs has launched a new team focused on policy research, to bridge the gap between AI research and global policymakers to make informed, scientific decisions about AI risks and capabilities.

Our research tackles the hardest problems in agent robustness, AI control protocols, and AI risk evaluations to help governments, industry, and the public understand and mitigate AI risk while maximizing AI adoption. This team collaborates broadly across industry, the public sector, and academia and regularly publishes our findings. We are actively seeking talented researchers to join us in shaping this vision.

As a Research Scientist working on Agent Robustness you will work on the fundamental challenges of building AI agents that are safe and aligned with humans. For example, you might:

  • Research the science of AI agent capabilities with a focus on how they relate to safety, risk factors, and methodologies for benchmarking them;
  • Design and build harnesses to test AI agents’ tendency to take harmful actions when pressured to do so by users or tricked into doing so by elements of their environment;
  • Design and build exploits and mitigations for new and unique failure modes that arise as AI agents gain affordances like coding, web browsing, and computer use;
  • Characterize and design mitigations for potential failure modes or broader risks of systems involving multiple interacting AI agents.

Ideally you’d have:

  • Commitment to our mission of promoting safe, secure, and trustworthy AI deployments in the industry as frontier AI capabilities continue to advance.
  • Practical experience conducting technical research collaboratively. You should be comfortable building and leveraging agent scaffolding, designing evaluation harnesses, and quickly turning new ideas from the research literature into working prototypes.
  • Experience with post-training and RL techniques such as RLHF, DPO, GRPO, and similar approaches.
  • A track record of published research in machine learning, particularly in generative AI.
  • At least three years of experience addressing sophisticated ML problems, whether in a research setting or in product development.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills to operate in a cross-functional team.

Nice to have:

  • Hands-on experience with agent evaluation frameworks such as SWE-bench, WebArena, OSWorld, Inspect, or similar tools.
  • Experience with red-teaming, prompt injection, or adversarial testing of AI systems.

Our research interviews are crafted to assess candidates' skills

Scale AI accelerates the development and deployment of AI, from the high-quality training data and evaluation services that power the world's leading AI labs, to full-stack AI applications built for Enterprise, U.S. Public Sector, and Global Public Sector customers. Scale's Global Public Sector team is focused on using AI to address critical challenges facing the public sector around the world. About Scale AI

Scale AI is the data foundation for AI, helping organizations build and deploy reliable production AI applications. We partner with the world's leading enterprises and government organizations to accelerate their AI transformation through frontier AI systems that solve real business problems.

Every day, we work with organizations across finance, healthcare, manufacturing, media and telecommunications to build production AI agents that automate complex workflows, help humans, reason over enterprise knowledge, and operate safely at scale.

Applied AI is moving faster than ever. New foundation models, reasoning techniques, agent architectures, and research papers emerge every week. Yet building AI systems that reliably solve real-world problems remains one of the hardest engineering challenges.

As a Staff Frontier Agent Engineer (Applied AI), you'll bridge the gap between cutting-edge AI research and production deployment. You'll work directly with enterprise customers to design, evaluate, and deploy intelligent systems that combine frontier models with structured knowledge, retrieval, traditional machine learning, and enterprise software.
